Not sure exactly what "substantially higher" means here.  In absolute terms yes, relative to GDP probably no.
Though likely it was more the fact that the licenses were auctioned and not freely awarded that really counted.
Among the best examples of how using tools of economics leads to can lead to the more efficient allocation of scarce resources.
